reuse.why: Builds on the existing WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule abstraction (adding isSkippedByWeekendRule and a shared isOffDay holiday check) and every call site, including the new range handler and the budget template, goes through it.

duplication.why: The 'walk occurrences, drop the ones isSkippedByWeekendRule rejects, look ahead by a heuristic margin' logic is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and the WeekendRule object literal is rebuilt from config at each site.

placement.why: Rule logic lives in shared/schedules.ts and handlers stay in server/schedules/app.ts, but the daily-skip occurrence iteration that belongs with the rule is left to each server/shared caller.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps; minor noise from an import reorder and two release notes.

maintainability.why: Callers must remember to combine isSkippedByWeekendRule with applyWeekendRule and pick their own look-ahead bounds (14+n, count*7+14+n, 3+n), and applyWeekendRule gained an odd fallback branch for invalid modes, so the rule is split across helper and call sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All weekend/holiday decisions go through applyWeekendRule, applyWeekendRuleToDay or isSkippedByWeekendRule; none re-tests weekends or holidays inline.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-and-look-ahead iteration appears as filter+slice with a reverse fallback in getNextDate, a counted for-of loop in getUpcomingDates, and a margin window with a Set in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays fields; applyWeekendRule gains a dropsWeekends early return and a separate invalid-solveMode fallback branch, and a second predicate isSkippedByWeekendRule that every caller must compose with it (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, schedule-template.ts).
